Figure 2.Comparison of three presentation-generation paradigms.
Programmatic methods preserve editability but offer limited visual creativity, while image-centric generation improves aesthetics at the cost of text fidelity and editability.SlidesWeavercombines both strengths, producing visually rich, granularly editable slides with an optimized cost-latency profile.

Figure 3.Overview ofSlidesWeaver, a multi-agent system for hybrid PPTX generation.
A shared Input & Deck Planning Phase establishes deck-level semantic, narrative, and visual context.
During Deck Generation, specialized agents follow two complementary routes:Topology Firstgrounds diffusion-proposed structure and adapts text to it, whileText Firstpreserves intended content and uses diffusion to guide and validate executable geometry.
Finally, the Visual Synthesis and Assembly Agents convert structured slide states into coherent visual layers and editable PPTX slides.

Figure 5.SlidesWeaverdominates Pareto-optimal configurations; the other two are low-cost AutoPresent variants that sacrifice performance.
We plot all 24 system-model configurations by cost, latency, and normalized composite quality; dark outlines mark Pareto-optimal points.

Figure 6.Qualitative comparison on a presentation request explaining model-free reinforcement learning through Doraemon and his gadgets.
All systems use GPT-5.4 as the language model, and GPT Image 2 is used whenever image generation is applicable.
From left to right, we showSlidesWeaver(Topology First),SlidesWeaver(Text First), AutoPresent, DeepSlides, DeepPresenter without/with image generation.
While the baselines predominantly rely on recurring text-card or text-image partitions,SlidesWeaverexhibits greater variation in grouping, hierarchy, and spatial composition across slides.
